owb_source: Open Word Bible (OWB), Balanced edition, Amharic
about: Read by library.requote (manage.py requote_inventory). Three things live here, all language data rather than code:

book_names: how the Amharic library cites each book, mapped to USFM. A numbered book is keyed with its ordinal ('1ኛ ቆሮንቶስ'); a citation written '1 ቆሮንቶስ' or '1ኛ ቆሮ.' is normalised to that key before lookup. Abbreviations are listed as their own keys, without the trailing dot.

fold: pairs of Ethiopic syllable rows that spell the same sound (ሐ/ኀ/ሀ, ሠ/ሰ, ዐ/አ, ፀ/ጸ). The 1962 text and OWB often spell one word with different rows, so the fuzzy 'is this the same verse' match folds them; the verbatim-OWB check never does.

decisions: the recurring-verse and recurring-word calls wave 1 settled (amowb/_TEMPLATE-wave2.md, 'Wave-1 recurring words'). The inventory flags every row whose reference matches one, or whose aligned English block holds one of its `english` phrases, or whose Amharic block holds one of its `old` words — so the worker reuses the decision instead of re-deciding it. Keep `english` phrases specific: a bare common word ('might', 'repent') flags half a book. A decision marked `detect` goes further: each of its `old` wordings becomes a row of its own (kind `recurring`, under its first reference) wherever it stands — for refrains too short for any detector to call Scripture by themselves.

decisions.decision: OWB calls the Spirit ጠበቃ (Advocate). Quote OWB; where the author argues from 'Comforter', add a one-time bridging gloss rather than rewriting his image.
OWB renders the divine name እግዚአብሔር. A quoted verse keeps OWB; the author's own 'Jehovah' in prose follows the same word.
OWB John 16:8 reads መሳሳቱን ያረጋግጣል; reuse that gloss where the author argues from 'convict'.
Isa 11:2 'might' is OWB ብርታት (የምክርና የብርታት መንፈስ).
'The promise' is ተስፋ, as OWB words it.

english: God is not a man, that he should lie
decisions.decision: OWB gives three different verbs for God 'repenting' (ተጸጸተ, አቋሙንም የሚለውጥ, ሐሳቡንም አይለውጥም). Quote each verbatim; one gloss in the author's prose covers all three.
1 Thess 5:17 is OWB «መጸለይን አታቋርጡ». The old «ሳታቋርጡ ጸልዩ» is OWB Colossians 4:2, so a block holding it under a 1 Thess 5:17 citation is NOT already OWB.
Murray's refrain 'Lord, teach us to pray' is OWB Luke 11:1's span «ጌታ ሆይ፣ … እንዴት መጸለይ እንዳለብን አስተምረን»; headings and body quote it identically.

The refrain «ፈቃድህ ትሁን» is the old wording. OWB Matt 26:42 ends «ፈቃድህ ይሁን»; Matt 6:10 has «ፈቃድህ በምድርም ይደረግ»; Luke 22:42 «የአንተ ፈቃድ ይሁን». Quote the span of the verse the author means, and keep a refrain identical everywhere it recurs.
OWB Luke 14:23 has አጥብቀህ ለምናቸው ('press them'). Where the author argues from 'compel', add a one-time gloss.
OWB Ps 141:5 says the opposite of the AV the author follows; Spurgeon's quotation stays self_rendered.

english: what wilt thou have me to do
decisions.decision: OWB Acts 9:6 lacks the KJV question. Quote OWB Acts 22:10 and cite Acts 22:10.
OWB reads ኩሽ. Where the author argues from 'Ethiopia', keep ኢትዮጵያ and mark the row self_rendered.
OWB reorders: 'good gift' becomes 'perfect gift'. Read the paragraph after the quote and adjust prose that argues from the old word.
OWB has 'bent reed / wick about to go out'. A one-time bridging gloss beats rewriting a recurring image.

OWB follows the critical text and lacks some or all of these words. Quote what OWB has; render the missing words from the English yourself and mark the row self_rendered (never keep the 1962 wording).

OWB reads «በኃጢአት አይቀጥልም» ('does not continue in sin'). Quote OWB wherever the author's sentence stays true. Where he argues AGAINST the 'continue/habitually' reading (Wesley's Christian Perfection, Great Privilege, Marks of the New Birth), render from the English («ከእግዚአብሔር የተወለደ ሁሉ ኃጢአትን አያደርግም፤ … ከእግዚአብሔርም ስለ ተወለደ ኃጢአትን ማድረግ አይችልም») and mark the row self_rendered. 1 John 5:18 'keepeth himself': OWB has 'the Son keeps him'; quote only «ክፉውም አይዘውም».

OWB Isa 27:3 reads «እኔ እግዚአብሔር የምንከባከባት ነኝ። በየጊዜው ውኃ አጠጣታለሁ» — 'continually', not 'every moment'. Murray argues from 'every moment' (Absolute Surrender, Abide in Christ). Quote OWB as it stands and let the author's own question carry the gloss («በየጊዜው» በእርግጥ በየቅጽበቱ ማለት ነውን?); his prose keeps በየቅጽበቱ.
OWB Zech 3:2 reads «ከእሳት የተነጠቀ የሚነድ ጉማጅ». A book title built on the phrase stays the title; body quotations take OWB's words, with a one-time «(ትንታግ)» bridge where the title word must be recognised.

english: the violent take it by force
decisions.decision: OWB reads the opposite sense (the kingdom suffers attack; violent men try to seize it). Where the author applies the AV to importunate prayer or holy violence (Bounds via Liddon; Wesley), render from the English and mark the row self_rendered.

english: All things are possible to him that believeth
All things are possible with God
decisions.decision: The refrain is OWB Mark 9:23 «ለሚያምን ሰው ሁሉ ነገር ይቻላል», identical wherever it recurs, unmarked recitations included. Its twin 'All things are possible with God' quotes OWB Matt 19:26 «ለእግዚአብሔር ግን ሁሉ ይቻላል», because OWB Mark 10:27 («እግዚአብሔር ሁሉን ማድረግ ይችላል») loses the parallel the author argues from.
OWB reads «ሄኖክ ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ተመላለሰ». Quote that wherever the text is quoted; the author's subject 'walking with God' may stay «ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር መሄድ» in prose (OWB 1 John 2:6 uses the same ተመላለሰ).
OWB Matt 5:8 reads «ልባቸው ንጹሕ የሆነ የተባረኩ ናቸው፤ እግዚአብሔርን ያያሉ». Quote that span wherever the beatitude is quoted, and 'blessed' as «የተባረኩ»; the running term «ንጹሕ ልብ» stays in the prose.

Bernard (On Loving God) builds three states — eat, drink, be inebriated — and the friends/dearly-beloved distinction on the Vulgate. OWB pairs 'drink' with 'lovers' and ends «ጠጥታችሁም እርኩ». Keep the Vulgate rendering, self_rendered; the half-verse 'I have drunk my wine with my milk' is OWB «ወይን ጠጄንና ወተቴን ጠጥቻለሁ».
OWB reads «ገና ልጅ ነኝ» in both verses; the refrain «ብላቴና ነኝ» is the 1962 wording. Quote OWB's phrase wherever it recurs, unmarked echoes included.
